page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose, 7th-generation instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a custom ARM64 processor based on the ARMv8 AWS Neoverse-V1 core design running at 2.6 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory is provisioned at 128.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 15 Gbps. There are no GPUs attached.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-core scalability and memory throughput. In Geekbench multi-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 17345.0, placing in the top 25%, while single-core performance registered in the average tier at 1488.0. Memory subsystems performed prominently, scoring 3104.66 in PassMark memory tests (top 10%) with uncached read-only bandwidth reaching 222.8 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 103.49 GB/sec. PassMark database operations and physics tests also reached the top 25%, as did static web serving throughput at 50.57 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded bzip3 decompression landed in the bottom 25% (8.65 GB/sec), and prompt processing on a 70B parameter LLM was constrained at 5.18 tokens/sec (bottom 10%).

The 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation provides consistent compute execution without hyperthreading contention, while the 1900 GB NVMe local instance store offers low-latency scratch space. Tradeoffs center on ARM64 instruction set compatibility and lower single-threaded throughput relative to dedicated high-frequency x86 compute instances. The instance architecture is best suited for general-purpose application backends, container orchestration, static web serving fleets, caching layers like Redis, and transactional database workloads that leverage local NVMe storage and high multi-core throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services m7gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with a 32-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 ARM64 processor running at 2.6 GHz with dedicated single-threaded cores. It integrates 128.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core), 1900 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, and a 15 Gbps baseline network link, operating without GPUs. Benchmark metrics reveal strong multi-threaded and memory subsystems, highlighted by a top 10% PassMark memory score of 3104.66, top 25% Geekbench multi-core performance (17345.0), and 50.57 GB/sec static web throughput. Single-threaded metrics and heavy LLM prompt workloads remain average to low. The balanced compute density and NVMe store make it suited for databases, caching, and containerized web infrastructure.
